units.en: Khitan territory lay five thousand li northeast of the capital, stretching east to Goguryeo, west to the Xi, south to Yingzhou, and north to the Mohe and Shiwei, with the Lengling range as their barrier. They hunted for a living and moved their camps at will. The Dahe chiefs commanded forty thousand warriors organized in eight tribes; they acknowledged the Turks as overlords and served as irkin. All tribes mustered for war, but each could hunt on its own. They feuded constantly with the Xi, usually lost, and retreated to the Xianbei Mountains. Early in the Wude era — the opening "chu" was originally written "zhong," corrected from the year-2 notice and Jiu Tang Shu 199b — Grand Chief Sun Aocao and the Mohe leader Tudi Ji presented themselves at court. In year 2 they raided Pingzhou. In year 6 Chief Zhuoluo offered fine horses and pelts. In Zhenguan year 2 Mo Hui surrendered; when the Turks asked to swap Liang Shidu for the Khitan, Taizong replied, "Khitan and Turk are not kin; Shidu is a subject household of Tang — I mean to take him — and I will not trade away those who have submitted." Mo Hui visited court in year 3, received drums and banners, and thereafter paid regular tribute. Campaigning against Goguryeo, the emperor drafted every Khitan and Xi leader. On the return through Yingzhou he appointed Kuge Left Martial Guard General. The grand chieftain Quju brought his people in; ruhezhu was his chiefly title, while the parallel account reverses the transmitted name Juqu to Quju. See Xin Tang Shu 219 and juan 32 note [7]. His band became Xuan Prefecture under Juqu, attached to Yingzhou. When Kuge led the whole tribe inward, Songmo Protectorate was founded: Kuge became protector, was enfeoffed Lord of Wuji, and received the surname Li. The Daqi became Qiaoluo Prefecture, Hebian Tanhan, Duhuo Wufeng, Fenwen Yuling, Tubian Rilian, Ruixi Tuhe, Zhuijin Wandan, and the Fu line the twin prefectures Pili and Chishan — all under Songmo, with their respective chieftains as prefects. After Kuge's death they rebelled with the Xi; campaigning general Ashide Shubin seized Songmo protector Abu Gu (A Bu Gu in Xin Tang Shu) and sent him to Luoyang. Kuge left two grandsons: Kumoli, Tanhan prefect and Prince of Guishun, and Jinzhong, Songmo protector. Aocao's great-grandson Wanrong — the line repeats; Jiu Tang Shu agrees; Xin Tang Shu reads "had a grandson Wanrong" — held Guicheng Prefecture. Yingzhou protector Zhao Wenbi bullied their people until Jinzhong and Wanrong rose together, killed Wenbi, seized Yingzhou, proclaimed themselves "Supreme Khans," and made Wanrong commander. Within twenty days they mustered tens of thousands, took Chongzhou, and captured suppression vice-commissioner Xu Qinji. Empress Wu sent Generals Cao Renshi and twenty-seven others, renaming Wanrong "Wan the Beheaded" and Jinzhong "Jin the Exterminated." At Huangzhang Valley west of Xiashi the imperial force was routed. They failed to capture Pingzhou. Wu sent more troops. Wanrong struck Tanzhou by night; Zhang Jiujie of the Qingbian command drove him off. Jinzhong soon died and Turk Mokchuo shattered the tribe. Wanrong regrouped. Lieutenants Luo Wuzheng and He Axiao entered Jizhou, killed prefect Lu Baoji, and carried off thousands. Learning of Jinzhong's death, Wu ordered Wang Xiaojie and one hundred seventy thousand men against Wanrong; at East Xiashi they were beaten, Xiaojie was killed, and Wanrong sacked Youzhou. Lou Shide followed with two hundred thousand; Wanrong marched south in full vigor and ravaged Yingzhou's counties. Shenbing commander Yang Xuanji — the text's Yang Liji is wrong per Xin Tang Shu — led Xi auxiliaries, crushed Wanrong, captured He Axiao, and accepted the surrender of Li Kaigu and Luo Wuzheng. Wanrong abandoned his army; Xuanji and the Xi closed in from four sides until his host broke and fled east. Zhang Jiujie laid three ambushes. Cornered, Wanrong fled east of the Lu River with a household slave; exhausted, he lay under trees while the slave took his head to Jiujie, who sent it to Luoyang. The Khitan remnant could not endure and joined the Turks. In Kaiyuan year 2 Jinzhong's cousin Shihuo brought the tribe back. : Shihuo received an iron certificate from Xuanzong. In Kaiyuan year 4 he came with Xi chief Li Dachi; the court restored Songmo, made Shihuo protector and Prince of Songmo, re-created the Jingxi Army, appointed him frontier commissioner, and made the eight chiefs prefects. In year 5 the Yang clanswoman became Princess Yongle and married him — per Jiu Tang Shu, "In Kaiyuan year 3 their chief Li Shihuo led his tribes to submit inward; the next year Shihuo entered court, and the emperor's clanswoman Yang was made Princess Yongle and given to him in marriage." He died in year 6. : Suogu, Shihuo's brother, inherited. In Kaiyuan 7/11 Suogu and the princess attended court. Yamen officer Ketuyu was bold and popular; Suogu tried to kill him, the plot failed, Ketuyu attacked, and Suogu fled to Yingzhou. Protector Xu Qindan and Xi lord Li Dachi attacked Ketuyu, failed, and both died. (Han Yu writes Ketugan; Liu Xu, Song Qi, and Tang Huiyao write Ketuyu.) : Yuyu, Suogu's cousin, was set up by Ketuyu, apologized to court, and Xuanzong confirmed him in Suogu's place. In Kaiyuan 10 Yuyu came to court; a Murong clanswoman became Princess of Yancheng and married him; he died. : Tuyu (Zhuoyu in this text; Tuyu in both Tang histories and Tongkao 345), Yuyu's brother, succeeded. In Kaiyuan 13 he quarreled with Ketuyu and fled with the princess; the court enfeoffed him Prince of Liaoyang (Commandery in both Tang histories). : Shaogu, Tuyu's brother — both Tang histories say Li Jinzhong's brother — was raised by the people. In Kaiyuan 13 winter he attended the mobile court, joined the Fengshan at Mount Tai, became Prince of Guanghua, and a Chen clanswoman became Princess Dongguang (Donghua in both Tang histories) and married him. In year 18 Ketuyu murdered him, led the people to the Turks, and the princess fled to Pinglu. : Qulie (Qulie in Xin Tang Shu; Zhang Jiuling's Qujiang ji 8 has Julei), lineage unknown, enthroned by Ketuyu. In Kaiyuan 22/6 Zhang Shougui of Youzhou — both histories say chief administrator; his title was "Vice Military Commissioner of Youzhou, Chief Administrator of Youzhou, and Censor-in-Chief," per Qujiang ji 9 — routed Ketuyu. In month 12 he won again, beheaded Qulie, Ketuyu, and others, sent heads to Luoyang; survivors hid in the hills. Guo-zhe (Yujie in Qujiang ji 5 and 8; guo may stand for yu) was a Khitan chief and Songmo yamen officer who killed Ketuyu and Qulie and submitted. Zhang Shougui made him Prince of Beiping. That year Ketuyu's follower Ni-li killed Guo-zhe and exterminated his house; son Lagan escaped to Andong as Left Xiaowei General. Thereafter the Khitan waned; the Dahe clung to the Xi king to reach Tang with yearly tribute: twice in Zhide–Baoying, thirteen visits in the Dali era (not "the twelfth year of Dali"; the era lasted fourteen years), thrice in Zhenyuan 9–11, seven in Yuanhe, four in Taihe and Kaicheng. Ni-li — Nieli in Yelü Yan, Yali in Chen Daren — was ancestor to Liao Taizu. Li Huaixiu, given Tang name and surname, Khitan name Dilian Zuli (Zuli above), was chief of the eight tribes. In Tianbao 4 he surrendered and became Songmo protector. An Lushan asked to campaign against the Khitan; the text says Huaixiu raised one hundred thousand — Xin Tang Shu says Lushan raised over one hundred thousand from four commands, not Huaixiu's army — and defeated Lushan south of the Huangshui, after which war with Lushan never ceased. Yelü Yan records that Taizu's fourth-generation forebear Noulishi, yilijin of the Yila, sent Zhiligu and Kulie to rout Fan Yang Lushan at the Huangshui in Huaixiu's day; Huaixiu was thus the first Yaolian lord and Zuwu Khan. Kai-luo, enfeoffed Prince Gongren, replaced the Songmo protector and was called Khitan king. The state grew; in Zhenyuan 4 it raided the north and Youzhou reported. After Lushan's rebellion Hebei warlords blocked the roads and many generations are lost — yet Officials Treatise 1 lists nine Yaolian khans in the Nine Accounts office. : King Qushu, in Huichang 2 made Cloud-Banner General, was Yelan Khan — the title was misplaced under a Youzhou commissioner entry and is corrected per Xin Tang Shu. Commissioner Zhang Zhongwu said the Khitan still used Uyghur seals and begged a new imperial seal inscribed "Khitan Serving the State" (Goryeo's record has Quxu). : King Xier (Xierzhi in Xin Tang Shu) was Bala Khan; in Xiantong he twice sent tribute and the tribes strengthened. : King Qinde of Xier's line was Hendejin Khan; in Guangqi he raided Xi and Shiwei until all served him and fought Liu Rengong repeatedly; late in life his rule failed. Great men of the eight tribes rotated every three years, but Yila chief Yelü Abaoji raised his own banners, refused rotation, called himself king, seized all Khitan lands, and ended the Yaolian. : Xiao Hanjianu held that after Yaolian Khan Wa the line broke until yilijin Yali enthroned the Zuwu Khan. Comparing Tang and Liao sources, the Dahe ended with Shaogu; Yali's enthronement was Huaixiu; only Qulie and Guo-zhe lay between. Qulie was Ketuyu's puppet; Guo-zhe, a collateral chief, was killed by Yali. Tang history calls Ni-li Ketuyu's remnant — so was Wa perhaps Qulie?
units.literal: The Khitan lands lay five thousand li northeast of the capital and were expansive; east they bordered Goguryeo, west the Xi, south Yingzhou, north Mohe and Shiwei, securing themselves behind the Lengling Mountains. They hunted and had no fixed dwellings. Their ruler of the Dahe clan had forty thousand effective troops, divided into eight tribes, and submitted to the Turks as irkin. Whenever mobilized for attack or war all tribes assembled; for hunting each tribe could act on its own. They were at odds with the Xi; whenever they fought they fared poorly and fled to shelter on the Xianbei Mountains. At the beginning of Wude — chu was originally zhong, corrected per the account below for year 2 and Jiu Tang Shu 199b Khitan Account — Grand Chieftain Sun Aocao and the Mohe chief Tudi Ji both came to court. In year 2 they invaded Pingzhou territory. In year 6 Chieftain Zhuoluo presented famous horses and rich sables. In Zhenguan year 2 Mo Hui came to surrender; the Turks asked to exchange Liang Shidu for the Khitan, and Taizong said: "The Khitan and Turks are not the same kind; Shidu is a Tang registered household — I will capture him — one cannot exchange a surrendered people." In year 3 Mo Hui entered court and was given drums and banners; thereafter there was regular tribute. When the emperor campaigned against Goguryeo he mobilized all Khitan and Xi leaders to follow the army. Returning through Yingzhou he made Kuge Left Martial Guard General. The ruhezhu Quju, a grand chieftain, led his people to submit — the transmitted name Juqu is reversed to Quju in the parallel account, while ruhezhu is the Khitan chiefly title; see Xin Tang Shu 219 and juan 32 collation [7]. His tribe was made Xuanzhou with Juqu as prefect, subordinate to Yingzhou Protectorate. Kuge brought his whole tribe to submit inward; Songmo Protectorate was then established with Kuge as protector, enfeoffed as Lord of Wuji, surname Li bestowed. The Daqi tribe became Qiaoluo Prefecture, the Hebian tribe Tanhan Prefecture, the Duhuo tribe Wufeng Prefecture, the Fenwen tribe Yuling Prefecture, the Tubian tribe Rilian Prefecture, the Ruixi tribe Tuhe Prefecture, the Zhuijin tribe Wandan Prefecture, the Fu tribe the two prefectures Pili and Chishan — all subordinate to Songmo, with their respective chieftains as prefects. When Kuge died they rebelled with the Xi; campaigning general Ashide Shubin seized Songmo Protector Abu Gu — Xin Tang Shu reads A Bu Gu — and presented him in the eastern capital. Kuge's two grandsons: Kumoli, Tanhan prefect and Prince of Guishun; Jinzhong, Songmo protector. Aocao's great-grandson was Wanrong — duplicated; Jiu Tang Shu agrees; Xin Tang Shu reads "had a grandson Wanrong" — Guicheng prefect. The Yingzhou protector Zhao Wenbi repeatedly insulted their subordinates; Jinzhong and others resented it and with Wanrong jointly raised troops, killed Wenbi, seized Yingzhou, styled themselves "Supreme Khans," and made Wanrong commander. Within twenty days their force numbered tens of thousands; they attacked Chongzhou and captured Vice Commissioner for Suppression Xu Qinji. Empress Wu was enraged and ordered Generals Cao Renshi and twenty-seven others to attack them, renaming Wanrong "Wan the Beheaded" and Jinzhong "Jin the Exterminated." At Huangzhang Valley west of Xiashi the imperial army was defeated. Advancing on Pingzhou they could not take it. Empress Wu sent more troops against the Khitan. Wanrong raided Tanzhou by night; Qingbian Circuit Vice Commander Zhang Jiujie resisted and Wanrong fled. Soon Jinzhong died and the Turk Mokchuo struck and broke their tribe. Wanrong gathered scattered troops and revived. Lieutenant-generals Luo Wuzheng and He Axiao entered Jizhou, killed Prefect Lu Baoji, and plundered several thousand people. Hearing Jinzhong had died, Empress Wu ordered Minister of Summer Works Wang Xiaojie and others with one hundred seventy thousand troops against Wanrong; at East Xiashi they were defeated, Xiaojie died, and Wanrong advanced to slaughter Youzhou. She also ordered Censor-in-Chief Lou Shide and others with two hundred thousand troops; Wanrong with sharp momentum marched south in drum-order and ravaged counties subordinate to Yingzhou. Shenbing Circuit Commander Yang Xuanji led Xi in a flanking strike — originally Shenbing Commander Yang Liji, corrected per Xin Tang Shu — greatly defeated Wanrong, captured He Axiao, and lieutenants Li Kaigu and Luo Wuzheng surrendered. Wanrong abandoned his army and fled; Xuanji and the Xi struck from four sides, Wanrong's host collapsed and fled east. Zhang Jiujie set three ambushes. Wanrong in extremity fled east of the Lu River with a household slave on light horses, utterly exhausted, lying under a grove; the slave cut off his head and presented it, and Jiujie sent it to the eastern capital. The Khitan remnant could not stand and attached to the Turks. In Kaiyuan year 2 Jinzhong's younger cousin Shihuo led the tribe back to Tang. : Shihuo — Xuanzong bestowed an iron certificate. Kaiyuan year 4 he came with Xi chief Li Dachi; an edict restored Songmo Prefecture, made Shihuo protector and Prince of Songmo, re-established the Jingxi Army, made Shihuo frontier commissioner, and the eight tribal chiefs all became prefects. Year 5 the Yang clanswoman was made Princess Yongle and married to Shihuo — per Jiu Tang Shu, year 3 Shihuo submitted, year 4 he attended court and the emperor's clanswoman Yang was made princess. Year 6 he died. : Suogu, Shihuo's younger brother — the emperor had Suogu inherit the title. Kaiyuan year 7 month 11 Suogu and the princess came to court. Yamen officer Ketuyu was fierce and won the people's hearts; Suogu wished to remove him; the plot leaked and Ketuyu attacked; Suogu fled to Yingzhou. Protector Xu Qindan and Xi lord Li Dachi attacked Ketuyu without success; Suogu and Dachi both died. (Han Yu writes Ketugan; Liu Xu, Song Qi, and Tang Huiyao all write Ketuyu.) : Yuyu, Suogu's younger cousin — Ketuyu pushed him as leader, sent envoys to apologize, and Xuanzong enfeoffed him to succeed Suogu. Kaiyuan year 10 Yuyu entered court; the Murong clanswoman was made Princess of Yancheng and married to Yuyu; he died. : Tuyu — written Zhuoyu in this text but Tuyu in both Tang histories and Tongkao 345 — Yuyu's younger brother, inherited office and title. Kaiyuan year 13 Tuyu again clashed with Ketuyu and fled to court with the princess, enfeoffed Prince of Liaoyang — both Tang histories read Prince of Liaoyang Commandery. : Shaogu, Tuyu's younger brother — both Tang histories read younger brother of Li Jinzhong — the people jointly enthroned him. Kaiyuan year 13 winter he attended the traveling palace, followed the Fengshan at Mount Tai, was changed to Prince of Guanghua, and the Chen clanswoman was made Princess Dongguang and married to Shaogu — both Tang histories read Donghua Princess. Year 18 he was assassinated by Ketuyu, who led his people to surrender to the Turks; Princess Dongguang fled to Pinglu. : Qulie — Xin Tang Shu reads Qulie; Zhang Jiuling's Qujiang ji 8 reads Julei — lineage unknown; Ketuyu enthroned him. Kaiyuan year 22 month 6 Youzhou Military Commissioner Zhang Shougui greatly defeated Ketuyu — both Tang histories read Youzhou Chief Administrator Zhang Shougui; his title then was "Vice Military Commissioner of Youzhou, Chief Administrator and Censor-in-Chief," per Qujiang ji 9. Month 12 he defeated them again, beheaded Qulie and Ketuyu and others, sent heads to the eastern capital; the remainder scattered into the valleys. Guo-zhe — Qujiang ji 5 and 8 read Yujie, 9 and 11 read Guo-zhe; yu and yu sound alike; guo should perhaps be yu — was originally a Khitan tribal chief, Songmo yamen officer, who beheaded Ketuyu and Qulie and submitted to Tang. Zhang Shougui enthroned him and enfeoffed him Prince of Beiping. That year Ketuyu's remnant Ni-li assassinated Guo-zhe and slaughtered his family; one son Lagan fled to Andong and was appointed Left Xiaowei General. From this the Khitan declined; the Dahe attached themselves as vassals to the Xi king to reach Tang, tribute coming yearly. Between Zhide and Baoying they came twice; in Dali thirteen times — originally miswritten Dali year 12, corrected per Xin Tang Shu; Dali had fourteen years, roughly once a year — Zhenyuan years 9–11 three times, Yuanhe seven times, Taihe and Kaicheng four times. Ni-li — Yelü Yan's Liao history writes Nieli, Chen Daren writes Yali — was the progenitor of Liao Taizu. Li Huaixiu, Tang bestowed name and surname, Khitan name Dilian Zuli — above written Zuli — originally great chief of the eight tribes. Tianbao year 4 he surrendered to Tang and was appointed Songmo protector. An Lushan memorialized to campaign against the Khitan; Huaixiu raised one hundred thousand troops — per Xin Tang Shu An Lushan raised more than one hundred thousand from Youzhou, Yunzhong, Pinglu, and Hedong; not Huaixiu's one hundred thousand — fought Lushan south of the Huangshui; Lushan was greatly defeated, and thereafter fighting with Lushan was unceasing. Yelü Yan's annals say Taizu's fourth-generation ancestor Noulishi as Yila tribe yilijin sent generals Zhiligu and Kulie to greatly defeat Fan Yang An Lushan at the Huangshui, exactly in Huaixiu's time; thus Huaixiu was clearly the first lord of the Yaolian and the Zuwu Khan. Kai-luo, enfeoffed by Tang as Prince Gongren, replaced the Songmo protector and was then called Khitan king. Thereafter they gradually grew; Zhenyuan year 4 they raided the northern frontier and Youzhou reported it. From Lushan's rebellion the Hebei was carved up and communications cut; generations cannot all be traced — per Officials Treatise 1 the Yaolian Nine Accounts Grand Constant already lists nine generations of khans. : Khitan King Qushu — in Wuzong's Huichang year 2 appointed Cloud-Banner General — this is Yelan Khan. The phrase "is Yelan Khan" was originally placed under "Youzhou Military Commissioner," mistaking Qushu for commissioner; corrected per Xin Tang Shu. Youzhou Commissioner Zhang Zhongwu memorialized that the Khitan formerly used Uyghur seals and begged a newly made imperial seal; an edict used the text "Khitan Serving the State." (Goryeo's ancient record writes Quxu.) : Khitan King Xier — Xin Tang Shu reads Xierzhi — was Bala Khan. In Xiantong he twice sent envoys with tribute and the tribes grew stronger. : Khitan King Qinde, of Xier's clan, was Hendejin Khan. In Guangqi he raided the Xi and Shiwei tribes and made them all serve; he repeatedly fought Liu Rengong. In his later years government declined. The eight tribal great men were by law replaced every three years; Yila tribe Yelü Abaoji raised banners and drums, made himself a separate tribe, refused rotation, styled himself king, possessed the whole Khitan state, and the Yaolian perished. : Xiao Hanjianu said that after the Yaolian Khan Wa the royal line was cut off, and from yilijin Yali enthroning the Zuwu Khan the great throne was first fixed. Comparing Tang and Liao histories now, the Dahe ended with Shaogu; Yali enthroned Huaixiu; between them were only Qulie and Guo-zhe. Qulie was enthroned by Ketuyu; Guo-zhe as collateral chief was killed by Yali. Tang history calls Ni-li Ketuyu's remnant; then Khan Wa was perhaps Qulie?

units.zh: 以翰林學士、中書舍人王溥為戶部侍郎充職，以左司郎中、充樞密直學士景範為左諫議大夫充職。
units.en: Wang Pu (Hanlin academician and Secretariat drafter) was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue; Jing Fan (Left Department director and military affairs direct academician) was appointed Left Remonstrance Counselor.
units.literal: Wang Pu, Hanlin academician and Secretariat drafter, was made Vice Minister of Revenue to fill the post; Jing Fan, Left Department director and concurrently direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made Left Remonstrance Counselor to fill the post.

units.zh: 時李嗣源總帳下親軍攻東北隅；
units.en: Li Siyuan led the household guard against the northeast corner;
units.literal: Li Siyuan commanded the personal troops below the tent attacking the northeast corner;

units.zh: 李嗣源壞夾城東北隅，率先掩擊，梁軍大恐，南向而奔，投戈委甲，噎塞行路，斬萬餘級，獲其將副招討使符道昭洎大將三百人，芻粟百萬。
units.en: Li Siyuan breached Jiacity's northeast and charged in; Liang panicked and fled south, shedding arms until the road jammed; over ten thousand were killed; Fu Daozhao and three hundred officers were taken, with a million bundles of fodder.
units.literal: Li Siyuan broke the northeast corner of Jiacity and led the assault; the Liang army was greatly terrified and fled south, casting weapons and armor; the road was choked; more than ten thousand were beheaded; deputy pacification commissioner Fu Daozhao and three hundred great generals were captured, and a million measures of fodder.

units.zh: 五月辛未朔，晨霧晦暝，帝率親軍伏三垂崗下。
units.en: At the xinwei new moon in the fifth month, thick morning fog hid Cunxu's personal troops below Sanchui Ridge.
units.literal: On the first day xinwei of the fifth month, morning fog dark and dim, the Emperor led his personal army in ambush below Sanchui Ridge.

units.zh: 己巳，秘書少監姚顗為左散騎常侍，以太子左諭德陸崇為右散騎常侍，以兵部郎中蕭希甫為左諫議大夫，前幽州節度判官呂夢奇為右諫議大夫，以鄴都副留守孫嶽為潁州團練使。
units.en: On jisi Yao Hui became Left Regular Attendant; crown prince mentor Lu Chong became Right Regular Attendant; Xiao Xifu of Military Affairs became Left Remonstrator; Lü Mengqi, former Youzhou aide, became Right Remonstrator; Sun Yue, Yedu deputy regent, became Ying training commissioner.
units.literal: On jisi, Vice Director of the Secretariat Yao Hui was made Left Regular Attendant; the crown prince's Left Mentor Lu Chong was made Right Regular Attendant; Bureau of Military Affairs director Xiao Xifu was made Left Remonstrator; former Youzhou military commissioner's aide Lü Mengqi was made Right Remonstrator; Yedu deputy regent Sun Yue was made Yingzhou training commissioner.

units.zh: 丙辰，以端明殿學士李專美為兵部侍郎，以端明殿學士李崧為戶部侍郎，以翰林學士馬裔孫為禮部侍郎，以禮部郎中、充樞密院直學士呂琦為給事中，並充職如故。
units.en: On bingchen Li Zhuanmei, Duanming Hall academician, was made Vice Minister of War; Li Song, Duanming Hall academician, was made Vice Minister of Revenue; Ma Yisun, Hanlin academician, was made Vice Minister of Rites; Lü Qi, Director of the Ministry of Rites and direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made Supervising Secretary—all retaining their concurrent posts.
units.literal: On bingchen, Li Zhuanmei, Academician of the Duanming Hall, was made Vice Minister of War; Li Song, Academician of the Duanming Hall, was made Vice Minister of Revenue; Ma Yisun, Hanlin Academician, was made Vice Minister of Rites; Lü Qi, Director of the Ministry of Rites and direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made Supervising Secretary—all retaining their concurrent posts.

units.zh: 以左拾遺、直樞密院李崧充樞密直學士。
units.en: Left Reminder Li Song, direct privy councilor, became privy council academician.
units.literal: Left Reminder and direct privy councilor Li Song became privy council academician.

units.zh: 丙辰，以秘書監呂琦為禮部侍郎，歸德軍節度使趙在禮改天平軍節度使，昭義軍節度使兼侍衛親軍馬步軍都虞候杜重威改忠武軍節度使，忠武軍節度使、侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使劉知遠改歸德軍節度使，前河陽節度使兼奉國左右廂都指揮使侯益改昭義軍節度使。
units.en: On bingchen Lü Qi, palace library director, became vice minister of rites; Zhao Zaili of Guide became Tianping military commissioner; Du Chongwei of Zhaoyi became Zhongwu military commissioner; Liu Zhiyuan of Zhongwu became Guide military commissioner; and Hou Yi, former Heyang commissioner, became Zhaoyi military commissioner.
units.literal: On bingchen, Lü Qi, Director of the Palace Library, was appointed Vice Minister of Rites; Zhao Zaili, Military Commissioner of the Guide Army, was changed to Military Commissioner of the Tianping Army; Du Chongwei, Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi and Chief Adjutant of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot, was changed to Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu Army; Liu Zhiyuan, Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu Army and Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot, was changed to Military Commissioner of the Guide Army; Hou Yi, former Military Commissioner of Heyang and Commander of the Left and Right Wings of the Fengguo Army, was changed to Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi.

units.zh: 帝召學士馬裔孫謂曰：「史在德語太凶，其實難容。
units.en: The Emperor summoned Academician Ma Yisun and said, "Shi Zaide's language is too harsh; it is in truth hard to tolerate.
units.literal: The Emperor summoned Academician Ma Yisun and said, "Shi Zaide's language is too harsh; in truth it is hard to tolerate.

units.zh: 爾代朕作詔，勿加在德之罪。」
units.en: Draft an edict for me and do not punish Zaide."
units.literal: You shall draft an edict for Us and do not impose punishment on Zaide."

units.zh: 詔曰：
units.en: An edict read:
units.literal: An edict stated:

units.zh: 丁卯，以西面行營馬步都指揮使、左龍虎軍統軍賀瑰為檢校太傅、同中書門下平章事，充宣義軍節度使、鄭滑濮等州觀察處置等使。
units.en: On dingmao, He Gui—Western Line horse-and-foot commander and Left Dragon-Tiger commander—was made honorary Grand Mentor and Grand Counselor and named Xuanyi military commissioner over Zheng, Hua, and Pu.
units.literal: On dingmao, Western Line camp horse-and-foot commander and Left Dragon-Tiger Army commander He Gui was made honorary Grand Mentor and Grand Counselor, and Xuanyi Army military commissioner and observation and disposition commissioner for Zheng, Hua, and Pu.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：時論平慶州功，故賀瑰進秩。）〉
units.en: The Zizhi Tongjian notes: Contemporary opinion credited the pacification of Qing Prefecture, so He Gui was advanced in rank.
units.literal: The Zizhi Tongjian notes: At the time, opinion credited the pacification of Qing Prefecture, and therefore He Gui was advanced in rank.

units.zh: 十二月，晉王自太原復至魏州。
units.en: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin returned from Taiyuan to Weizhou.
units.literal: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin came again from Taiyuan to Weizhou.

units.zh: 陝州節度使張延朗移鎮許州，加檢校太傅；
units.en: Zhang Yanlang of Shaan moved to Xu with inspector grand mentor rank;
units.literal: Shaan prefecture military commissioner Zhang Yanlang was transferred to Xu prefecture and given added Inspector Grand Mentor;

units.zh: 天復初，帝密語韓偓曰：「陸扆、裴贄孰忠於我？」
units.en: Early in the Tianfu era, the emperor spoke privately to Han Wo and asked, "Between Lu Yi and Pei Zan, which of them is more loyal to me?"
units.literal: Early in Tianfu the emperor spoke secretly to Han Wo: "Lu Yi and Pei Zan—which is more loyal to me?"

units.zh: 偓曰：「扆等皆宰相，安有它腸？」
units.en: Wo replied, "Yi and the others are all chancellors. How could they harbor any other intent?"
units.literal: Wo said: "Yi and the others are all chancellors—how could they have other designs?"

units.zh: 偓曰：「孰為陛下言此？」
units.en: Wo asked, "Who told Your Majesty this?"
units.literal: Wo said: "Who told Your Majesty this?"

units.zh: 偓曰：「設扆如是，亦不足責。
units.en: Wo said, "Even if Yi had done as alleged, he would not deserve blame.
units.literal: Wo said: "Even if Yi were so, he would not deserve blame.

units.zh: 且陛下反正，扆素不知謀，忽聞兵起，欲出奔耳。
units.en: Moreover, when Your Majesty restored the throne, Yi had known nothing of the plot. When he suddenly heard that fighting had broken out, he simply wished to flee.
units.literal: Moreover when Your Majesty restored the throne, Yi never knew of the plot. Suddenly hearing troops rise, he wished only to flee.

units.zh: 陛下責其不死難則可，以為不喜，乃讒言也。」
units.en: Your Majesty may blame him for not sharing the peril of the moment, but to say that he was displeased with your restoration is nothing but slander."
units.literal: Your Majesty may blame him for not dying with the hardship, but to say he was displeased is slander."
